concerns.concern: The fitted dirty-limit slope of 16.3 pH·K/Ω is about 4–12× larger than the model's parameter-free prediction. The paper does not acknowledge this, so the linear correlation with Rs/Tc does not establish the dirty-limit mechanism.
concerns.quote: The measured 16.3 pH·K/Ω is therefore ~4–12× too large. The paper never mentions this

concerns.concern: The dirty-limit formula in Eq. 2/24 drops the factor of π from the Mattis–Bardeen result that the SI itself derives in Eq. 23. This changes the expected slope by a factor of π.
concerns.quote: This π is not a convention issue: it is lost between two consecutive lines of the SI.

concerns.concern: The clean-limit term is treated as a constant 80 pH instead of scaling as 1/d. This yields an unphysical ratio of 0.7 (below 1), and the headline 0.7→15 enhancement is an artefact; a proper A/d treatment gives a ratio of about 2.5 for the thinnest film.
concerns.quote: The headline 0.7→15 progression is an artefact of using a constant clean term.

concerns.concern: The 'monolayer' device D1 is most likely a bilayer. AFM gives ~2 nm, a shear mode is present (it is absent in a monolayer), and the stated Raman relation gives N ≈ 1.8, not 1.5.
concerns.quote: The device is therefore most plausibly a bilayer.

concerns.concern: D1's Rs and Tc are taken from literature data for atomically thin NbSe2 rather than matching its likely bilayer nature. This single point dominates the linear fit in Fig. 4c and also drives the 1/d fit.
concerns.quote: That single point dominates the linear fit in Fig. 4c

concerns.concern: Rs and Tc are paired from different DC flakes or from literature rather than measured on the microwave devices. If disorder is sample-specific, as the paper claims, this pairing cannot test the mechanism device by device.
concerns.quote: Under that hypothesis, pairing across samples cannot test the mechanism device by device.

concerns.concern: A ratio of 15 for the thinnest film implies a mean free path of about 0.6 nm. This contradicts the ~15 nm mean free paths quoted from transport.
concerns.quote: that gives l ≈ 0.6 nm, contradicting the ~15 nm mean free paths quoted from transport

concerns.concern: The SI fit in Fig. S5b gives a slope of about 10, inconsistent with the 16.3 in Fig. 4c.
concerns.quote: roughly 700 pH / 68 Ω/K ≈ 10 in Fig. S5b, versus 16.3 in Fig. 4c

concerns.concern: The assumed λ = 230 nm conflicts with the paper's own Lk,sq data, which imply λ ≈ 1 µm and much larger Pearl lengths. The 'confinement-enhanced' Pearl-regime interpretation therefore rests on an inconsistent λ.
concerns.quote: The invocation of 'confinement-enhanced' Lk in the Pearl regime is therefore built on an inconsistent λ.

concerns.concern: The Pearl-regime condition (width much smaller than the Pearl length) fails for the thick devices D10–D12, whose Pearl lengths are comparable to their widths. The claim therefore does not hold for all samples.
concerns.quote: the '10-70 µm' range only covers d ≲ 10 nm, so 'all of our NbSe2 samples' is incorrect.

concerns.concern: The claim of one of the highest sheet kinetic inductances at comparable thickness is contradicted by Fig. 4b. There, TiN, NbTiN and grAl films exceed NbSe2 at similar thicknesses.
concerns.quote: The claim is not supported by the figure, except perhaps as a statement about the thinnest device alone.

concerns.concern: The extraction attributes all termination inductance to kinetic inductance. For the thick devices, the geometric inductance of the strip and contacts may be comparable to the extracted 8–14 pH.
concerns.quote: so these values may be dominated by geometry.

concerns.concern: Control-resonator frequencies vary by an amount equivalent to about 0.2 nH, larger than most extracted Lk values. It is not stated whether each control is on the same chip or how this enters the uncertainties.
concerns.quote: That spread is equivalent to ~0.2 nH, larger than most of the extracted Lk.

concerns.concern: The Kerr derivation has a sign error: quantizing the current rather than flux gives a positive K, whereas a current-increasing inductance must give a negative K.
concerns.quote: This gives a positive K in Eq. 8, but a current-dependent inductance that increases with I lowers the frequency, so K must be negative.

concerns.concern: The quoted Kerr value of −3.8 Hz cannot be reproduced from the stated inputs, which give about 5.7 Hz.
concerns.quote: gives |K|/2π ≈ 5.7 Hz, not 3.8 Hz.

concerns.concern: A factor-of-2 to 3 discrepancy between the calculated and measured Kerr coefficient (−1.7 Hz) is described as good agreement.
concerns.quote: a factor-of-2 to 3 discrepancy with the measured −1.7 Hz is described as 'good agreement'

concerns.concern: The participation of the lumped NbSe2 termination in the distributed λ/4 mode is not discussed in the Kerr analysis.
concerns.quote: the participation of a lumped termination in a distributed λ/4 mode is not discussed.

concerns.concern: The assumed 1 nm per layer conflicts with the NbSe2 interlayer spacing of about 0.63 nm. This makes the layer axis of Fig. 4a and the labels in Table S3 questionable.
concerns.quote: The 2H-NbSe2 c-axis lattice constant is ~1.25 nm per two layers, i.e. ≈0.63 nm per layer.

concerns.concern: The shear-mode frequency saturates for thicker flakes, so distinguishing 7, 8 and 9 layers by Raman would require sub-0.3 cm⁻¹ precision. That precision is not demonstrated.
concerns.quote: Distinguishing 7, 8 and 9 layers this way requires sub-0.3 cm⁻¹ precision, which is not demonstrated.

concerns.concern: Comparing this device's Kerr coefficient to granular Al and Josephson junction arrays is not like-for-like, because Kerr depends on mode participation and geometry. A geometry-normalized figure of merit is needed.
concerns.quote: A self-Kerr coefficient is a property of a mode, not of a material.

concerns.concern: A quadratic Lk(I) is generic for any fully gapped superconductor. It cannot be taken as evidence for anisotropic nodeless pairing.
concerns.quote: It does not discriminate anisotropic nodeless pairing from isotropic s-wave.

concerns.concern: Fig. 4c lacks horizontal error bars reflecting the Rs/Tc uncertainty, such as the sample-to-sample spread among same-thickness devices.
concerns.quote: The x-axis uncertainty also appears nowhere in Fig. 4c.

concerns.concern: The Pearl-length formula in SI Eq. 27 is misprinted as 2λ/d, which is dimensionless.
concerns.quote: SI Eq. 27 writes Λ = 2λ/d, which is dimensionless

concerns.concern: Table S3 lists ratios of 1.79 and 1.75 for Lk,sq = 135 pH, whereas 135/80 = 1.69.
concerns.quote: Table S3 lists 1.79 and 1.75 for Lk,sq = 135 pH, whereas 135/80 = 1.69.

concerns.concern: The quoted Kerr range in the conclusions drops the minus sign on 14.7. It also does not match Table 1, which lists −0.006 Hz values smaller in magnitude than the stated lower bound.
concerns.quote: The quoted range therefore does not match the data table.

concerns.concern: The D6 frequency difference is given as 0.45 GHz, but the stated resonance frequencies give 0.55 GHz. This is the one worked example in the main text.
concerns.quote: the difference is 0.55 GHz, not 0.45 GHz.

concerns.concern: The dirty-limit penetration depth in Eq. 19 contains a stray µ0 factor, so it does not have units of length.
concerns.quote: Eq. 19 includes a stray factor µ0, so λdirty would not have units of length.

concerns.concern: The onset power of the power-induced downshift is −90 dBm in the text but −100 dBm in the Fig. 3b caption.
concerns.quote: The main text places the onset of the power-induced downshift at −90 dBm (green arrow), while the Fig. 3b caption gives −100 dBm

concerns.concern: The text says the DC bias was swept up to 30 µA, but Figs. 3e–f show data only to about 15 µA.
concerns.quote: The text says the bias was swept 'up to IDC = 30 µA', but Figs. 3e–f show data only to ~15 µA.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 3a label (−100 dBm, Qi = 2×10⁴) does not match the text's description of a single-photon measurement with Qi = 2.8×10⁴.
concerns.quote: Fig. 3a is labelled Pin = −100 dBm and Qi = 2×10⁴. The text instead describes a single-photon-limit measurement with Qi = 2.8×10⁴
